header: Date: 2026-06-10 | Time: 10:00 UTC | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), David Chen (Redwood SE), Anika Rao (Redwood CSM), Maya Singh (Horizon CTO), Evan Torres (Horizon Eng Mgr), Priya Patel (Horizon Security), Omar Ruiz (Horizon SRE)
transcript:
[00:00] Lena Park: Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on, quick check-in. We saw the incident yesterday around 14:23 UTC, I wanted to walk through what we know and what we plan to do. Maya, do you want to start with how it showed up on your side?
[00:12] Maya Singh: Yeah thanks, um so our customer facing search and checkout API had a burst of timeouts and some 5xx spikes, roughly 14:20 to 14:45, it impacted about 1.3% of requests during a promo. The errors were timeouts to the Redwood endpoint and then a handful of 502/503s. We retried on our side which seemed to exacerbate the spike.
[00:38] David Chen: Got it. On the Redwood side, preliminary telemetry shows a concurrent connection surge and corresponding worker memory pressure on one node group, a handful of kernels hit OOM and restarted which leads to transient 5xxs. There's also a pattern where client retries land on same set of hot workers.
[00:56] Evan Torres: Right, our logs show we had a retry window of 0-3 with immediate retry, no exponential backoff for that route, so we were effectively retrying rapidly.
[01:07] Priya Patel: Quick security note — we will need any logs with PII redacted; also retention window for trace data for this pilot is important for compliance.
[01:17] Lena Park: Absolutely, Priya — we'll share filtered traces. David, can you confirm the retention policy on the pilot cluster and whether traces include headers we need to redact?
[01:26] David Chen: For the hosted pilot cluster, default trace retention is 14 days, and we can produce filtered exports with header redaction. If you want longer retention we can discuss, but for this investigation 14 days should be enough.
[01:36] Omar Ruiz: From SRE perspective we want to know the exact request IDs and time ranges so we can correlate with our load balancer and client-side retries. I can pull the LB logs once I have IDs.
[01:47] Lena Park: Perfect, Omar — action: send request IDs. We'll also push a config change suggestion for retries and circuit breaker.
[01:54] Maya Singh: Can you explain what the recommended immediate mitigation is? We're worried about another promo tomorrow.
[02:00] David Chen: Short answer: add a modest exponential backoff with jitter on client retries and enable a circuit breaker on the route to avoid retry storms hitting the same worker pool. Also increase the token-bucket burst size on the Redwood rate limiter for that peak window and configure worker autoscale burst to avoid OOMs.
[02:20] Evan Torres: Increasing burst size sounds good but we worry about costs. What's the trade-off?
[02:25] Lena Park: Cost vs reliability — dedicated burst capacity or temporary higher concurrency increases cost, but you avoid customer-facing errors. For the pilot I'd recommend temporary burst and a narrow time window tied to the promo. We can show cost delta after the replay test.
[02:39] Priya Patel: Also need to confirm encryption and KMS for logs if we extend retention. For a later private deployment we'd want KMS & HSM support.
[02:49] David Chen: We support KMS-backed encryption for private deployments; hosted pilot has envelope encryption and we can integrate your KMS under Private if you move to VPC later. For this POC we can provide redacted traces under Redwood's keys or an export for you to ingest.
[03:06] Lena Park: Okay let's talk concrete next steps: David will share traces and a config diff with retry/backoff and token-bucket tweaks. Omar will send sample request IDs. We'll run a replay test. Any objections or extra asks?
[03:20] Maya Singh: One ask — can you include per-token latency breakdown? We saw tail latency spikes and want to know if it's KV cache misses or attention kernel latency.
[03:31] David Chen: Yes will include per-token timing and a heatmap; that should show cache-hit vs miss and token-level kernel timings.
[03:40] Evan Torres: On the replay test, can we simulate our spike pattern (heavy reads, some long contexts up to 2k tokens)? We want realistic load.
[03:50] David Chen: We can. We'll coordinate on exact QPS and sequence length distribution. For initial run suggest 10k QPS equivalent with same pattern; if that looks good we can run scaled runs.
[04:02] Priya Patel: If we find persistent 5xx after tuning, what's the escalation path? We need an incident timeline and contact for SLA invocation.
[04:11] Lena Park: Anika will own that. For pilot customers we have an escalation runbook and can offer a dedicated on-call SE during promo windows if needed.
[04:21] Anika Rao: I'll share the runbook and the SLA contact details in CRM after this call.
[04:27] Maya Singh: Also, you mentioned KV cache pressure — do you have configuration to tune cache TTLs or shard KV cache differently?
[04:36] David Chen: Yes, we can adjust KV cache TTL and increase cache shard count for hot endpoints. That reduces backend attention kernel work for repeated prefixes.
[04:45] Evan Torres: Any chance to do a canary rollout of the retry policy and rate limit change so we don't touch prod-wide?
[04:51] Lena Park: Absolutely — Redwood supports per-route canary and A/B rollout; we can push the retry policy to 10% first and monitor.
[05:00] Omar Ruiz: Great. For the logs I'll pull IDs and send them to David by end of day tomorrow.
[05:06] Lena Park: Perfect. Quick note on instrumentation — please make sure client request IDs are propagated in the x-request-id header so traces stitch cleanly.
[05:14] Maya Singh: We do propagate x-request-id, but some older frontends didn't for certain legacy routes; we'll double-check.
[05:22] Evan Torres: Timeline recap? We need the replay by June 16 and config diff by June 14?
[05:29] Lena Park: Yes: logs/IDs by June 11 (Omar), traces and initial analysis by June 12 (David), config diff by June 14 (David), replay test on June 16, follow-up sync June 17.
[05:40] Priya Patel: For compliance I'll need a note on what fields are in the trace export — can you include that in the initial email?
[05:47] Anika Rao: Will do, I'll attach a sample export schema and the runbook.
[05:52] Maya Singh: One more question — are rate limits applied per-account or per-API-key? We have both shared key and per-tenant keys.
[05:59] David Chen: In this pilot it's per-API-key by default, but we can do per-tenant aggregation if you want to avoid single-key hotspots.
[06:08] Evan Torres: That sounds helpful, we'll list hot tenants.
[06:12] Lena Park: Great — if no one has anything else we'll wrap. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up in email with the artifacts and schedule.
[06:21] Maya Singh: Thanks all.
[06:23] Lena Park: Thanks, bye.
